SUMMARY: hairstyle a straight waist-length fall of hair with a clean side part and two small temple braids; costume silhouette a long silk shawl wrapping the shoulders and arms and floating in the air, light layered robes — an airy, celestial silhouette; design idea Three broad shawl folds end in offset pairs across the back, suggesting the broken and unbroken lines of a trigram.; face original Yu Fan design; expression original Yu Fan design.
A full-body character image, vertical 2:3 (1024×1536): Yu Fan of the Romance of the Three Kingdoms, reimagined as an adult woman — the scholar exiled to the far south for speaking too plainly.

1. STYLE
Korean MMORPG character artwork. A recognisably drawn face with gently simplified anatomical structure. 2D painting with visible brushwork: layered strokes of colour, soft broken edges, thin coloured linework and a few crisp accents on the face and costume.
Her face is small and soft: a short midface, a softly rounded jaw and a small chin, about 1.3 times as long as it is wide, with her eyes open at their natural size. Bangs, side locks and headpieces frame the face without lengthening it.
Skin finish: dewy, glass-like highlights on the skin of her shoulders, arms, collarbones and legs — a soft, luminous wet-look sheen that follows the body's forms; her face keeps a soft, natural finish.

2. CHARACTER
Age: mid-twenties — a clear adult face.
Face — her own, recognisably this character, a woman's face with no beard or facial hair: a sharp, striking, intense look; light warm-beige skin with a golden undertone; softly tapered face narrowing to a small, soft chin; medium-sized eyes — long phoenix eyes with lifted outer corners, outer eye corners slightly lifted; thick straight brows; upturned nose; full heart-shaped lips; magenta eyes; a small beauty mark under one eye.
Body and hair: slender-limbed yet full-busted with rounded hips and a narrow waist build; a straight waist-length fall of hair with a clean side part and two small temple braids; bright amethyst-purple hair.
Expression: a cool, unimpressed look, subtle and relaxed.
Legend, carried in her design and bearing: brilliant and blunt, Book of Changes scholarship, a scholar's robe.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME AND EQUIPMENT — THREE KINGDOMS
Costume: a Han court official's dress — layered robes with a broad belt and a hanging seal cord, a black jinxian guan cap, an ink brush and bound bamboo slips. Late-Han Chinese dress — cross-collared silk robes with wide sleeves and a broad sash, lamellar or scale armor laced with cords where armor is worn, bronze, jade and lacquer ornament, Han court hair ornaments; silk, lacquered leather, bronze and iron.
Silhouette: a long silk shawl wrapping the shoulders and arms and floating in the air, light layered robes — an airy, celestial silhouette. This silhouette sets the overall shape of the costume above — keep its materials, ornaments and rank in this shape; the details are free.
Design idea: Three broad shawl folds end in offset pairs across the back, suggesting the broken and unbroken lines of a trigram.
Colours: crimson red, gold, river teal, black lacquer.
Signature item: a Book of Changes scroll. She holds it at full scale: one whole object, drawn once, held in front of or beside her body; a long weapon keeps one straight, unbroken shaft with a single head or blade.
Exposure (bold): her robes open to show skin — the cross collar opened into a deep neckline with natural cleavage, bare upper arms above detached wide sleeves (and bare shoulders where no shoulder guard sits), the skirt panels cut with a high side slit at full length — it shows the side line of one leg as she stands, no leg pushed out or knee bent for it; any armor pieces stay on and symmetrical. Intimate areas covered; keep the costume material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: Eastern Wu along the Yangtze, around 200–280 AD: the river capital Jianye, great war junks with crimson sails, river fortresses, southern rain and lotus marshes, the fire ships of the Red Cliffs.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Stance and hands: Her left forearm cradles the rolled scroll while the right hand rests open over the sash.
Setting detail: A river archive balcony under clear daylight, with lotus marshes and low timber piers behind.
Light: a soft key light with a strong rim light tracing her hair, shoulders and armour; bright, crisp specular highlights on metal and jewellery, and a clean, warm-neutral sheen on her skin.
Composition: her whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet inside the frame with clear margins, about four-fifths of the image height; camera at chest height with natural portrait perspective.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only — no second character, horse or other creature. No readable text or numbers, except that a banner, seal or emblem may carry the single character 吳 or 虞. No logo, watermark, speech bubble or frame border. Three Kingdoms-era Chinese dress, architecture and materials only.
Avoid: a blue or bruise-like tint on the skin around the eyes, glossy or shiny highlights on the face, sweaty, oily or plastic-looking skin.

후한 관복과 강가 기록 누각, 오 깃발 한 글자, 삼각선 주름의 숄이 보인다.
오른손은 허리띠에 있고 왼손은 이어진 죽간 두루마리를 잡는다.
깊은 목선, 드러난 어깨와 치마 옆트임이 요청에 맞는다.
